packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-09 - unverified blind image reading

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification or earlier reading of this text was in my
  context. Modern pencil notes on the pieces themselves read approx.
  "Stams, STA, Frag. 146-1r" (image-004, right piece) and "Stams, STA,
  Frag. 146-1v" (image-007, right piece); also a similar pencil note on the
  left strip (image-003, image-006). These are holding notes, not a text
  identification.
- Beyond the brief: to read the two upside-down strips I made rotated
  (180 deg), contrast-enhanced, 2x enlarged crops of image-002, image-006 and
  image-007 in the session scratchpad with a small local script. Line numbers
  for those strips are counted from the top of the UPRIGHT (rotated) strip.
  All other images read directly. No web/search/catalogue/edition used;
  packet.json not opened.
- While reading I recognised that some short phrases resemble wording of a
  familiar liturgical/biblical text; I have NOT used that to fill gaps and I
  give no identification. Everything below is what I see; where letters are
  not clear they are marked uncertain.

LAYOUT SURVEY
- Two faces, each photographed as two separate pieces (overviews image-001
  = face "1r" per pencil, image-005 = face "1v"). image-002..004 are tiles of
  face 1r; image-006..008 of face 1v.
- Each face: (A) a narrow horizontal strip on the left that lies UPSIDE DOWN
  relative to (B) a larger piece on the right with a small tab/stub below it.
  The strips are cut along a ruled boundary (red horizontal line at the
  strip edge). Pieces were probably used in a binding (observation of shape;
  interpretation).
- Script: a small, rounded late caroline / early gothic-looking book hand,
  brown ink, moderate abbreviation, single text block visible per piece;
  column edges truncated on at least one side of each piece.
- Red features: red ruled vertical line in the margin; small red marginal
  notes "ac" (with two dots/strokes above) and a single "c"/"h" against
  certain lines; red underlining of short phrases within the text (these
  look like quoted lemmata underlined in red, followed by explanatory prose -
  tentative interpretation: text with underlined lemmata + commentary).
  One large red initial "O" on the stub of face 1v (image-008).
- No running titles visible. No interlinear glosses noted.

AREAS SELECTED: all legible lines of all four pieces (they are small).
UNREAD: lowest faded lines of the face-1v right piece (image-008 lines 9-11)
and the stub text on face 1r (image-004, stub line 1). Suggest a raking-light
or UV shot of image-008 lower third and the face-1r stub.

CONVENTIONS: (x) expansion; word? uncertain; [illegible]; [...] text cut by
the edge. <u>...</u> = underlined in red in the MS. "&" = tironian et.

==================== FACE 1r ====================

        --- stub below piece B ---
008.12  [illegible, abraded]

008.14  ...s oculi? [...]
Left of piece B (image-007/008): blank dirty parchment margin with pencil
"Stams, STA, Frag. 146-1v"; two holes.

LIMITATIONS
- Very small pieces; every line is truncated on at least one side. Strips A
  are separated from pieces B, and I have not established how the strip
  lines relate to the B lines (different parts of the leaf, inverted).
- Abbreviation expansions are tentative throughout; several key words
  (u03 "Nullus s(us)t(ine)t?", 002.u01 opening word) are uncertain.
- Lower lines of image-008 and the face-1r stub are faded/abraded.
- Face labels 1r/1v are taken from the modern pencil notes only.
